title: Generalis elementaria introductio (= Eclogae propheticae)
author: Eusebius of Caesarea
source: Translated by Claude from tlg2018.tlg023.1st1K-grc1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: .. ὑπειλήφασιν· τοὺς μὲν γὰρ μὴ ὁμολογοῦντας αὐτὸν .......... Θεὸν σαφῶς ὁ προφητικὸς διελέγχει λόγος τε .............. ὡς ἄρα αἱ ἐξόδοι αὐτοῦ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξ ἡμερῶν α...... ..... νουσι· τοῖς δὲ κατὰ Μαρκίωνα καὶ τὰς λοιπὰς .............. σεις πεπλανημένοις καὶ μὴ ὁμολογοῦσιν αὐτ ........... ρʹ καγένεσιν, μὴ δ’ ὅτι ἔγνωστο ὑπὸ τῶν τοῦ δημιου......... ν παραθετέον τὸν προφητευόμενον τῆς γενέσεως . ..
passages.english: [...] they have supposed. For those who do not confess him [...] God, the prophetic word clearly refutes [...], [saying] that his goings forth are from the beginning and from the days of [eternity] [...]; but to those who have been led astray in the manner of Marcion and the remaining [here]sies, and who do not confess his [...] birth, nor that he had been known by those of the Creator [...], one must set beside [this] the prophesied [place] of his birth [...].
passages.notes: The passage is badly lacunose, and several gaps cannot be restored with confidence. 'From the days of [eternity]' is restored from the quotation of Micah 5:2 in the context before ('from the days of ages'). 'Heresies' is restored from the fragment '...σεις', and 'Creator' from 'δημιου...' (i.e. the Demiurge, the Creator God, whom Marcion distinguished from the Father of Christ). The word 'καγένεσιν' seems corrupt or fragmentary: it may be part of a word for 'birth according to the flesh' or for a human birth. In the last clause the noun governed by 'prophesied' is lost; the following context, which mentions the place in Bethlehem, suggests 'place'. The opening refutation is probably aimed at the Artemonites, the Samosatene (Paul of Samosata) and the Ebionites named in the context before, who deny that Christ existed before the incarnation.

passages.original: Καὶ δὴ κατὰ τὸ ἕκτον αὐτοῦ τῆς ἀρχῆς ἔτος, ὅπερ ἦν ἀπὸ Κύρου τεσσαρακοστὸν καὶ ἕκτον, τὰ τῆς οἰκοδομῆς ἀποπληροῦται· ὅθεν ὁρμώμενοι τῷ Σωτῆρι ἡμῶν ἔλεγον, μ’ καὶ ἓξ ἔτεσιν ᾠκοδομήθη ὁ ναὸς οὗτος, καὶ σὺ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερεῖς αὐτόν; Κατὰ δὲ τὸν Ἰώσηπον ο’ (θ’) καὶ μ’ ἔτη ἀκριβῶς τὰ ἀπὸ Κύρου ἐπὶ τὸ Δαρείου ἔνατον ἔτος συνάγεται, ἐν ᾧ τέλος ἐπιθεῖναι τῇ τοῦ ναοῦ οἰκοδομῇ ἐν τῷ ἑνδεκάτῳ τῆς Ἀρχαιολογίας φησὶν αὐτολεξεὶ δηλῶν οἰκοδομηθήσεσθαι τὸν ναὸν ζ′ (sic) μηνὶ τοῦ ἐνάτου τῆς ἐπὶ Δαρείου βασιλείας ἔτους·
passages.english: And indeed in the sixth year of his reign, which was the forty-sixth from Cyrus, the work of building is completed. Starting from this, they said to our Saviour, "This temple was built in forty-six years, and will you raise it up in three days?" But according to Josephus, exactly forty-nine years are reckoned from Cyrus to the ninth year of Darius, in which he says, in the eleventh [book] of the Antiquities, that the building of the temple was brought to completion, stating in so many words that the temple would be built in the seventh (sic) month of the ninth year of the reign of Darius.
passages.notes: The numeral in the edition reads ο’ (70) with θ’ (9) given in parentheses as a correction; together with μ’ (40) the corrected reading gives 49, which fits the seven weeks of years in the context, and the translation follows it. The edition marks ζ′ (seventh) month with 'sic'. 'Of his reign' refers to Darius.
